speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, can you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; since you mentioned the symptoms are more pronounced on the right side, does this ataxia follow a specific progression, or did it start suddenly? Also, have you noticed any difficulty with speech or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab use.

The combination of subacute, asymmetric limb ataxia and a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suspicious for PML. I need to confirm if you have noticed any recent changes in vision or memory, and I will immediately request brain imaging to evaluate for white matter lesions.
